Prerequisite: A valid FortiPAM license: the FortiPAM-VM annual subscription license (the licensed user seats) uploaded to the VM, or the license of a hardware model
What it enables: Operation beyond evaluation mode (2 users, 15 days, no valid serial number, no FortiCare support); when the subscription expires, only Super Administrators can log in, FortiPAM goes into maintenance mode, and secrets cannot be launched
How to put it in place: Register the license registration code on FortiCloud and download the license file; GUI: System > FortiPAM License (Upload License File, in maintenance mode); on the 1000G and 3000G, enter the stackable seat license key in the same pane
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Licensing" (evaluation mode, "Registering and downloading your license", "Uploading the license file to FortiPAM-VM", "Subscription license") and "FortiPAM license" (stackable seat license for hardware models)

Prerequisite: An Advanced Malware Protection license (AVDB and DLP), included in the FortiPAM-VM subscription and bought separately as an annual contract for hardware models
What it enables: Antivirus signature updates and the DLP feature for file transfers and file secrets (DLP stops working when the license expires; antivirus scanning and DLP are not supported under the evaluation license)
How to put it in place: Buy the contract and register its code; GUI: System > FortiGuard License (Enter Registration Code)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Licensing" ("Advanced Malware Protection (formerly AntiVirus and DLP license)"; evaluation mode) and "Renewing FortiPAM-VM license"

Prerequisite: Maintenance mode, entered by an administrator whose role has Set Maintenance Mode
What it enables: Firmware upload, license upload, TPM and private data encryption changes on FortiPAM-VM, and log and video disk encryption, which are allowed only in maintenance mode
How to put it in place: config system maintenance; set mode enable; end
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "FortiPAM installation" (to update a firmware image, enter maintenance mode), "FortiPAM license", "FortiPAM with TPM" (FortiPAM-VM must be in maintenance mode to change TPM settings), and "Configuring log and video disk encryption" (disk operations only in maintenance mode)

Prerequisite: A log disk and a dedicated video disk: on FortiPAM-VM, two hard disks added to the VM before the image is installed
What it enables: Local log storage, session video recording, live recording, video watermarks, disk usage monitoring, and disk encryption of the log and video disks
How to put it in place: Add the two disks in the hypervisor before installation and check their usage (log and video) in the CLI after the first boot; GUI: Log & Report > Disk Usage
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "FortiPAM appliance setup" (administrators need to configure a dedicated video disk for video recording; two hard disks must be added to the VM) and "Disk usage"

Prerequisite: A TPM on the hardware unit, or a vTPM on FortiPAM-VM (KVM with the vTPM package, VMware, or GCP; vTPM is not supported on OCI)
What it enables: TPM protection of the private data encryption key for the secret credentials
How to put it in place: On hardware, check the TPM with diagnose tpm selftest; on FortiPAM-VM, add the vTPM in the hypervisor, then config system global; set v-tpm enable; end
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "FortiPAM with TPM" (on FortiPAM-VM, TPM can only be enabled after enabling vTPM), "Installing vTPM package on KVM and adding vTPM to FortiPAM-VM", "vTPM for FortiPAM on VMware", "Installation on GCP" (Enabling vTPM), and "Installation on OCI" (vTPM and disk encryption not supported)

Prerequisite: At least 4 GB of memory on a formal license (2 GB on an evaluation license)
What it enables: TPM or vTPM with private data encryption, and log and video disk encryption
How to put it in place: Allocate the memory to the VM in the hypervisor, or use a hardware model that has it
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "FortiPAM with TPM" and "Configuring log and video disk encryption" (when using TPM or vTPM and disk encryption, use 4 GB of memory on a formal license)

Prerequisite: A server certificate issued by the DoD PKI (or another approved CA) for the FortiPAM FQDN, with its private key, and a DNS name for that FQDN
What it enables: DoD-issued certificates for the GUI portal and FortiPAM's other HTTPS services, and FIDO2 passkeys, which work only when the GUI is reached through an FQDN with a trusted certificate
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Certificates (Create/Import: Generate CSR, have the DoD CA sign it, then import the signed certificate)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Certificates" ("Generating a CSR (Certificate Signing Request)") and "User registering a passkey" (FIDO2 requires an FQDN with a trusted certificate)

Prerequisite: The DoD root and intermediate CA certificates (and the CA certificate of any other server FortiPAM connects to over TLS) imported as CA certificates
What it enables: Validation of LDAPS and STARTTLS servers, of HTTPS backup servers, and of the user certificates presented for certificate authentication
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Certificates (Create/Import: CA Certificate, from a file or online SCEP)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Importing CA certificate", "LDAP servers" (Certificate, when Secure Connection is enabled), and "Authentication settings" (CA Certificate: trusted CA certificates that validate client certificates)

Prerequisite: Current certificate revocation lists of the DoD CAs
What it enables: Revocation data for the certificates FortiPAM trusts
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Certificates (Create/Import: CRL, File Based or Online Updating over HTTP or LDAP)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Importing a CRL (Certificate revocation list)"

Prerequisite: User certificates issued by the DoD PKI (CAC or PIV) to the users who log in with certificates, presented by their browsers
What it enables: Certificate authentication for FortiPAM login (7.0.0)
How to put it in place: Issue the certificates through the DoD PKI and make them available to the users' browsers; FortiPAM validates them with the CA certificates (P8)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Authentication settings" (client certificates presented during certificate authentication) and "What's new in FortiPAM" (certificate authentication for FortiPAM login)

Prerequisite: A remote LDAP directory (such as Microsoft Active Directory) that offers LDAPS or STARTTLS, with a bind account that can search the distinguished name
What it enables: Remote LDAP users and administrators, LDAP user import, and group matching for authorization
How to put it in place: Create the bind account in the directory; GUI: User Management > LDAP Servers (Server IP/name, Secure Connection, Protocol, Certificate, Username, Password; Test connection)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "LDAP servers" (setting up remote LDAP authentication) and "Importing LDAP users"

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider (such as FortiAuthenticator or another IdP) that enforces DoD PKI or MFA, signs its assertions and responses, and sends the user and group attributes
What it enables: SAML single sign-on for remote users, signed assertion checking, and the SCIM service, which works with SAML and auto provision rules
How to put it in place: Register FortiPAM as a service provider on the IdP and exchange metadata; GUI: User Management > Saml Single Sign-On (upload the IdP metadata or enter the IdP entity ID, URLs, and IdP certificate)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "SAML Single Sign-On (SSO)" (FortiPAM acts as the SP; IdP metadata; additional SAML attributes) and "SCIM service"

Prerequisite: A RADIUS server, with a shared secret for FortiPAM, that returns the Message-Authenticator attribute
What it enables: Remote RADIUS users and the Message-Authenticator check
How to put it in place: Add FortiPAM as a client on the RADIUS server; GUI: User Management > Radius Servers (IP/Name, Secret, Credential Status test)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "RADIUS servers" and "Message-Authenticator support for RADIUS"

Prerequisite: A remote user group that names the LDAP, RADIUS, or SAML server (P11, P12, or P13) where the remote users are found
What it enables: Remote users and administrators, and auto provision rules that map remote groups to roles
How to put it in place: GUI: User Management > User Groups (a remote group with the remote server)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "LDAP servers" (adding the LDAP server to a user group), "User groups", "Creating a user" (for Remote User, select a remote group), and "Auto provision rules"

Prerequisite: A SCIM client (the identity provider's provisioning service) that can reach the FortiPAM SCIM port and trusts FortiPAM's SCIM server certificate
What it enables: SCIM-driven provisioning, updating, and deprovisioning of users and groups
How to put it in place: Configure the SCIM URL that FortiPAM generates on the SCIM client; GUI: User Management > SCIM Service (Host, Service port, Server Certificate)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "SCIM service" ("Creating a SCIM client": the SCIM URL must be configured on the external SCIM client; the port must be reachable; the server certificate must be trusted by the SCIM client)

Prerequisite: FortiTokens (hard tokens or FortiToken Mobile tokens) added to FortiPAM and assigned to the users; two FortiTokens are available by default
What it enables: Two-factor authentication with FortiToken for local users
How to put it in place: GUI: User Management > FortiTokens (Create: serial numbers of hard tokens, or activation codes of mobile tokens; Activate)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "FortiTokens" and "Creating a user" (Token, mandatory when the authentication type is FortiToken)

Prerequisite: An SMTP server that FortiPAM can send through (the Fortinet mail server is used by default), and an email address on each user who receives alerts
What it enables: Email alerts (critical system, glass breaking, and license expiry), automation stitches that send email, FortiToken activations, and email notifications to users
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Settings (Email Settings, Email Service: Use custom settings with the organization's SMTP server, SMTPS, and Sender; Test Connection)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Settings" (Email Service: email alerts, FortiToken activations, and guest management credentials), "Email alert settings" (by default, the Fortinet mail server is used), and "Testing the email service connection"

Prerequisite: A mailbox on an IMAP server (or Microsoft Graph) that FortiPAM can poll for approval reply emails
What it enables: Approval of secret requests by replying to the approval request email
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Settings (Approval Email Server: Email Server Address, Email Pulling Server Address, Email Pulling Service Port, User Name, Email Folder, Server Certificate)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Settings" (Approval Email Server), "Approving secrets by Email", and "Approval email using Microsoft Graph"

Prerequisite: A central syslog server (or SIEM, such as FortiSIEM) reachable from FortiPAM
What it enables: Off-loading of the system and secret logs to syslog
How to put it in place: GUI: Log & Report > Log Settings (Send logs to syslog, IP Address/FQDN; Edit in CLI for mode and port)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Log settings" ("Configuring parameters to send logs to syslog server")

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer, or FortiAnalyzer Cloud, that authorizes FortiPAM
What it enables: FortiAnalyzer logging, logs stored on FortiAnalyzer with an upload interval, and FortiAnalyzer Cloud logging
How to put it in place: GUI: Network > Fabric Connectors (FortiAnalyzer Logging or Cloud Logging: Status Enabled, Server; verify the serial number and authorize FortiPAM on FortiAnalyzer)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Fabric Connectors" ("FortiAnalyzer logging" and "FortiAnalyzer Cloud logging")

Prerequisite: An SFTP server for session videos, with an account (password or key pair) and the storage folder already created
What it enables: Session videos moved to external storage, with key-based authentication
How to put it in place: Create the account and the folder on the server; GUI: System > Backup (Remote Video Storage: Server, Server Port, Username, Authentication Method, Storage Path; Video Storage Mode Rolling)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Backup" (remote video storage: the folder must already exist on the storage server; works only when the Video Storage Mode is Rolling)

Prerequisite: A backup server (SFTP or HTTPS preferred; FTP and HTTP are also supported) with an account for FortiPAM
What it enables: Automatic configuration backups, with server certificate checking and key-based SFTP authentication
How to put it in place: Create the account on the server; GUI: System > Backup (Configuration Backup)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Backup" (automatic and periodic backup to an FTP, SFTP, HTTP, or HTTPS server; "Sending backup file to a server")

Prerequisite: DoD-approved NTP servers reachable from FortiPAM
What it enables: Time synchronization to authoritative time sources
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Settings (Set Time NTP, Select Server Custom); custom NTP server details must be configured in the CLI, and the guide does not print the command
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Settings" (System time; custom NTP server details must be configured via the CLI) and "System information widget"

Prerequisite: An SNMP manager that supports SNMP v3 with SHA-2 and AES, with the FortiPAM MIBs, and SNMP management access on the interface it uses
What it enables: SNMP v3 queries and traps
How to put it in place: GUI: Network > Interfaces (Management Access: SNMP on the interface the manager connects to); GUI: System > SNMP (Download FortiPAM MIB File)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "SNMP" (the SNMP manager must be listed as a host; SNMP must be selected in the interface's administrative access; Fortinet MIBs)

Prerequisite: One or two more FortiPAM units of the same model and firmware version (VMs on the same platform), with licenses registered to the same account, static interface addresses, and a heartbeat link
What it enables: An active-passive HA cluster and its cluster password
How to put it in place: GUI: System > HA (Mode Active-Passive, Group name, Password, Heartbeat interfaces, on each unit)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "High availability" (same device model and version; cross-platform HA is not supported; all nodes' licenses registered to the same account; interfaces must not use DHCP)

Prerequisite: A FortiClient EMS (7.2.0 or later) with Privilege Access Management enabled, connected to FortiPAM and authorizing it
What it enables: ZTNA tags and ZTNA-based access control to FortiPAM, to secrets, and to folders
How to put it in place: GUI: Network > Fabric Connectors (FortiClient EMS: IP/Domain name, HTTPS port; authorize FortiPAM on the EMS); config endpoint-control fctems; edit <EMS_NAME>; set server <EMS_ADDRESS>; next; end
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "FortiPAM deployment options" (EMS 7.2.0 or later), "Fabric Connectors", and "ZTNA user control" (the endpoint must connect to the same EMS server)

Prerequisite: Standard FortiClient (7.2.0 or later) with the ZTNA and PAM features on the users' Windows endpoints, registered to the same EMS as FortiPAM
What it enables: ZTNA endpoint control for logins and secret launches (ZTNA is not available with standalone FortiClient, the browser extension, or no client)
How to put it in place: Install FortiClient with ZTNA and PAM enabled, or push the installer package from the EMS
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "FortiPAM deployment options", "Feature availability" (ZTNA only with standard FortiClient), and "Installing FortiClient with the FortiPAM feature"

Prerequisite: The Fortinet Privileged Access Agent browser extension (Chrome or Edge) or FortiClient on the users' endpoints
What it enables: Proxy mode and direct mode web browsing through the FortiPAM web proxy, which are not available without a client
How to put it in place: Install the extension from the Chrome Web Store or Microsoft Edge Add-ons, or install FortiClient
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "FortiPAM deployment options" and "Feature availability" (web browsing not available with FortiPAM only)

Prerequisite: Targets reachable from FortiPAM (directly or through a secret gateway) over the protocol of the template's password changer (for example SMB for the Windows Machine template with the SAMBA changer, or LDAPS for Windows AD), with accounts whose passwords FortiPAM may change
What it enables: Automatic password changing and verification, password change at check-in, and password changing over LDAPS
How to put it in place: Open the protocol on the target's firewall and set the target's password policy to accept FortiPAM's changes; GUI: Secret Settings > Password Changers
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Automatic password changing" (a password changer linked to a secret template), "Password changers", and "Troubleshooting a secret that uses Windows Machine template" (the target has opened SMB in the firewall; minimum password age)

Prerequisite: WinRM enabled on the Windows targets, and a privileged account secret with WinRM access for each target
What it enables: RDP event logs, the dependency updater, Windows application filters and Windows Remote App, and JIT privilege scripts on Windows targets
How to put it in place: Run the WinRM setup script from FortiPAM on the target (HTTPS listener recommended) and allow ports 5985 or 5986; GUI: Secrets > Secrets (Privileged Account enabled on the secret of the privileged Windows account)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "WinRM configuration for Windows server", "Creating a secret" (a privileged account is needed for agentless RDP session log retrieval and the dependency updater), "Dependency updater", "Windows app control" (Prerequisites), and "Just-In-Time (JIT) privilege via Secret checkout/check-in (PowerShell)"

Prerequisite: A secret gateway device: a FortiGate or FortiProxy as a forward gateway, a FortiGate 7.6.3 or later or a FortiPAM as a reverse gateway, or a FortiPAM on the same image version (1.5.0 or later) as a service gateway
What it enables: Distributed architecture with forward, reverse, and service gateways
How to put it in place: GUI: Network > Secret Gateway (create the gateway and configure the gateway device)
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Secret gateway" (forward and reverse types; FortiGate 7.6.3 or above as a reverse gateway; not supported on FortiGate hardware models with 2 GB RAM from FortiOS 7.4.4; service gateway requirements)

Prerequisite: An approval profile with approvers other than the requester
What it enables: Requires Approval to Launch Secret in secret policies
How to put it in place: GUI: Secret Settings > Approval Profile
Source: FortiPAM 7.0.0 Administration Guide, "Policies" (Requires Approval to Launch Secret: approvers defined in the approval profile) and "Approval profile"
